evals.prompt: I'm new to testing. I want to develop a FastAPI endpoint POST /predict that will internally call a _load_model() helper and a _preprocess_image() helper before returning a JSON prediction. How should I structure my tests for this? I want to write the failing tests first, then write the code that makes them pass.
evals.expected_output: TDD-framed explanation: write failing tests anchored to the endpoint's observable behavior (HTTP status, response JSON shape) before implementing the endpoint. Should name test files/functions after behaviors, explain that internal helpers are tested indirectly through the endpoint, and give at least one concrete failing test example that drives the implementation.

evals.prompt: Every time I rename or split a class my tests break even though the behavior didn't change. Here's my test file: evals/files/test_trainer.py — what's wrong with it?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the structural coupling red flags: TestModelTrainer mirrors ModelTrainer class, tests call private methods (_build_optimizer, _run_epoch, _save_checkpoint), test names describe implementation not behavior. Explains why this causes fragility. Proposes behavior-anchored alternatives (e.g. test_training_reduces_loss, test_fit_produces_checkpoint) with at least one rewritten example.

evals.prompt: How many test files should I have? I have 12 production modules so I have 12 test files. Is that correct?
evals.expected_output: Explains that one-test-file-per-module is a structural coupling smell. Number of test files should match the number of user-facing behaviors, not production files. May have fewer test files than production modules. Illustrates with an example of collapsing multiple module-tests into one behavior-test file.
